CANONICAL_NAME.value: TinySTM -- a lightweight word-based software transactional memory (Felber, Fetzer, Riegel, Marlier; 2007-)

VERSION.value: github.com/patrickmarlier/tinystm master as of 2026-09-12 (commit in hashes; 1.0.5 lineage)

value.lineage: Software transactional memory (Shavit & Touitou 1995) as the research lineage that competed with lock-based concurrency in the multicore decade: TinySTM (2007, Univ. Neuchatel / TU Dresden) uses time-based validation (Riegel), encounter- or commit-time locking, and ships micro-benchmarks (bank, intset) that count aborts/commits. The human record: STM lost the mainstream to fine-grained locks and lock-free structures, survived in Haskell/Clojure and Intel TSX -- a partly SUPERSEDED design, preserved.

HUMAN_PROBLEM.value: composable atomic memory updates without locks

value.built_to: let threads compose memory operations into atomic transactions that abort and retry on conflict instead of holding locks
value.pressure: contention (conflicting transactions abort), memory reordering, the cost of validation
value.success_means: the bank's total balance is invariant under any interleaving; aborts are bounded and retried

value.pressure: resource contention, competing writers, retry cost
value.failure_condition: abort storms under high contention (livelock-like) or a validation bug that commits a conflicting transaction

cut.note: software transactional memory with a global version clock: every memory word maps (by address hash) to a lock word that is either owned (pointing at the writer's write-set entry) or free and carrying the version at which the word was last committed; a transaction reads a word only if its version is within the transaction's validity range, and if not, tries to EXTEND the range to the current clock by re-validating its whole read set; at commit it takes a new timestamp from the clock, validates the read set once more (unless nothing else committed meanwhile), writes back its buffered values and releases the locks with the new version; three designs (write-back with locks taken at encounter or at commit, write-through) and four contention managers are compile-time switches

organs.human_name: stm_internal.h 165-250: OWNED_MASK, WRITE_MASK, INCARNATION_MASK, LOCK_GET_TIMESTAMP(l) = l >> LOCK_BITS, LOCK_GET_ADDR, LOCK_GET_INCARNATION; the lock array indexed by address hash; GET_CLOCK on a global counter
organs.mechanism: a fixed array of lock words covers memory by hashing addresses to stripes; a word's low bit says whether it is owned by an in-flight writer, in which case the rest is a pointer to that writer's write-set entry (so a reader can find the owning transaction and, in write-through mode, the old value), otherwise the high bits are the version (the global clock value at the last commit that wrote the stripe) and a small incarnation count guards against a released-and-reacquired lock looking unchanged
organs.output: a lock word to read or CAS
organs.state: the lock array; the global clock
assumptions: a global clock is cheap enough (one atomic increment per commit) and gives a total order of commits; striping trades false conflicts for table size
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: validation is a comparison of integers, not a re-read of values (the time-based STM idea)
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the clock is a contention point on many cores; hash collisions between unrelated addresses cause false aborts
organs.human_prior: Riegel, Felber & Fetzer 2006 (LSA) and Dice, Shalev & Shavit 2006 (TL2): the two time-based designs this body generalises
organs.source_boundary: the lock-word macros and the clock

organs.human_name: stm_wbetl_validate (38-80): for each read entry, if the lock is owned by another transaction fail, else if its timestamp differs from the recorded version fail; stm_wbetl_extend (90-110): now = GET_CLOCK; if validate then tx->end = now
organs.mechanism: a transaction records for every read the stripe's version; validation walks the read set and fails if any stripe is now owned by someone else or carries a different version; a transaction whose read would need a version newer than its current upper bound does not abort immediately but tries to extend: it reads the clock, validates, and if nothing it read has changed it adopts the new bound (its snapshot is still consistent as of now); commit validates once more unless the transaction's start equals the new timestamp minus one (nobody committed in between)
organs.output: valid / invalid; a new end time
organs.update: on a version miss and at commit
assumptions: most reads of a long transaction stay valid, so extension avoids the aborts a fixed snapshot (TL2) would suffer; validation cost is linear in the read set, paid rarely
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: longer transactions survive concurrent commits (LSA's advantage over TL2)
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: validation is O(read set) per extension, so a transaction that keeps missing pays quadratically; a conflict callback exists for tracking
organs.source_boundary: validate, extend and the commit-time check

organs.human_name: stm_wbetl_commit (852-930): t = FETCH_INC_CLOCK + 1; if start != t - 1 and !validate then rollback; write back the write set; release locks with LOCK_SET_TIMESTAMP(t); the read-only fast path under CM_MODULAR; the irrevocable-transaction gate
organs.mechanism: writes were buffered in the write set with their stripes locked at encounter time (write-back, encounter-time locking); at commit the transaction increments the global clock to obtain its commit timestamp; if any other commit happened since it started it re-validates its reads (else the snapshot cannot have been invalidated); on success it copies each buffered value to memory and stores the new timestamp into each stripe's lock word, which releases the lock and publishes the version in one store; on failure it rolls back (releasing locks with the old versions) and retries per the contention manager
assumptions: holding write locks from encounter to commit makes commit cheap and detects write-write conflicts early; the clock increment is the linearisation point
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: atomicity and isolation for arbitrary code with no lock discipline from the programmer
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: irrevocable (non-abortable) transactions need a global gate; long write sets hold locks long
organs.human_prior: TL2's commit with the LSA clock

rejected_cuts.candidate: the read paths (invisible and visible reads 162-555), the write path (556-780), rollback, the write-through (stm_wt.h) and commit-time-locking (stm_wbctl.h) designs, the contention managers (suicide, delay, backoff, modular), the modules (logging, statistics, ordering, callbacks), epoch garbage collection (gc.c), the ABI wrappers, the tests
rejected_cuts.note: the contention-manager switch (CM_*) is a mechanism family of its own (who backs off, who wins)

rejected_cuts.evidence: the lock encoding, validation/extension and commit are separable and the body ships three designs over the same pieces

pressures.source_evidence: stm_internal.h lock words; stm_wbetl.h validate / extend / commit
pressures.condition: an organism executes blocks of memory operations from many threads with atomicity and isolation; conflicts are rare but real; some transactions are long and read-mostly; the score is throughput and the abort rate vs a fine-grained lock baseline
pressures.resource_or_constraint: a lock table; one global counter
pressures.failure_condition: lost updates or torn reads (safety), or an abort rate that makes long transactions starve
pressures.world_punishes: value-based validation (re-reading everything); a fixed snapshot for long readers; a global lock
pressures.world_rewards: versioned stripes with a global clock, snapshot extension, encounter-time write locks
pressures.observable_consequence: throughput and aborts on a red-black tree and a linked list benchmark vs threads, for TL2-style (no extension) vs LSA-style (extension), and vs fine-grained locks
pressures.cheat_control: an organism with a global lock must show zero aborts and no scaling; the no-extension variant must show more aborts on long read-mostly transactions; the extension variant must reduce them at the cost of validation time: the world must show all three
pressures.purpose_separated_from_pressure: PURPOSE: software transactional memory (Felber, Fetzer, Riegel 2008; TinySTM 1.0)
